Risk Statement: External attacker exploits WordPress vulnerability leading to website defacement, malware injection, and potential customer data exposure
Asset: Website + Customer database (loyalty program)
Threat Actor: External attacker or automated scanner
Vulnerability: Outdated WordPress version, no security plugin, auto-updates disabled, no WAF
Impact Description: Website down for hours, customer data exposed, POPIA s22 notification to the Information Regulator and affected customers may be required, reputational damage, lost sales
Current Controls: WordPress is installed (username documented), staff monitor occasionally
Control Gaps: No automated updates; no security plugin; no backup process; no malware scanning; no incident response plan
Recommended Controls: 1) Enable WordPress auto-updates, 2) Install security plugin (Wordfence or Sucuri free), 3) Implement Cloudflare WAF (free), 4) Daily backups to external drive, 5) Regular security scans
Notes: WordPress vulnerabilities actively exploited; high priority fix. Cost: <$100/year for plugins. Recovery time if infected: 2-4 days

Risk Statement: Employee accidentally posts customer loyalty data or payment information on social media leading to privacy breach and customer notification
Asset: Customer loyalty database; payment system
Threat Actor: Unintentional employee disclosure on public social media (TikTok/Instagram/Facebook)
Vulnerability: Lack of data classification policy, no social media policy, no employee training on data privacy, no approval process for customer-related posts
Impact Description: Customer names and email posted publicly, potential fraud risk, POPIA notification required, reputational damage, customer churn
Current Controls: No documented policy; employees know not to post but informal
Control Gaps: No data classification; no training; no social media guidelines; no monitoring
Recommended Controls: 1) Create data classification policy (draft from template), 2) Mandatory privacy training for all staff (1-hour session), 3) Social media policy requiring approval before posting customer info, 4) Monthly review of cafe's social media accounts
Notes: Preventable with training. Low cost (<$500). Test with simulated scenario post.

Risk Statement: Disgruntled or terminated employee steals customer loyalty database containing names, emails, point balances, potentially enabling fraud or account takeover
Asset: Customer loyalty database in server
Threat Actor: Disgruntled employee or recently terminated employee
Vulnerability: Access controls not enforced; terminated employees' access not immediately revoked; no separation of duties; no audit logging of database access
Impact Description: Customer accounts compromised, potential fraud, customer data sold, reputational damage, customer loss
Current Controls: Passwords protect database (weak), manual off-boarding process
Control Gaps: No tracking of who accessed what; no audit logs; no automated off-boarding; access not revoked same day
Recommended Controls: 1) Implement role-based access control (owner vs. manager vs. staff tiers), 2) Automated off-boarding (revoke all system access within 1 hour of termination), 3) Enable database audit logging of all access, 4) Monthly access reviews by owner
Notes: Critical for HR/IT coordination. Test by simulating employee termination.

Risk Statement: Weak POS password stored on sticky note under register compromised leading to unauthorized transactions, payment card fraud, or system compromise
Asset: POS system + Payment card data
Threat Actor: External attacker (social engineering to find sticky note), physically present threat, POS malware vendor
Vulnerability: Weak password (single word?), stored insecurely on sticky note, no MFA, outdated POS software, no encryption of payment data in transit or at rest
Impact Description: Payment card fraud ($10K+), PCI DSS violation ($5K-$25K fine minimum), criminal investigation, customer fraud, operational downtime (unable to process payments)
Current Controls: POS password exists (written on sticky note under register), basic username/password authentication
Control Gaps: No MFA; no vault for credentials; outdated software; no encryption; no access logging; no change log; no monitoring
Recommended Controls: 1) Move password to secure password manager (Bitwarden free or KeePass), 2) Enable MFA on POS system, 3) Update POS software, 4) Enable encryption of payment data (PCI DSS requirement), 5) Remove sticky note immediately, 6) Audit logs of POS access
Notes: Highest priority—payment card data is most regulated. Cost: <$200. Compliance audit requirement.

Risk Statement: WiFi credentials compromised due to single known password leading to unauthorized network access, malware spread, or customer/business data theft
Asset: WiFi Network + Customer data + Business data on server
Threat Actor: Unauthorized user (customer on public WiFi; attacker; disgruntled employee)
Vulnerability: WiFi password known to many people, no change mechanism documented, open/unencrypted WiFi for customers, no network segmentation (customer WiFi on same network as staff systems), no monitoring of connected devices
Impact Description: Unauthorized access to customer data, malware spread to staff computers, ransomware, data breach, network downtime
Current Controls: WiFi password shared verbally with staff and some customers, router exists but unclear who manages it
Control Gaps: No change process; no documentation; no segmentation; no monitoring; no WPA3 encryption
Recommended Controls: 1) Change WiFi password immediately (strong password), 2) Document change process, 3) Implement separate WiFi for customers (SSID: CafeGuest) and staff (SSID: CafeStaff) using router feature, 4) Use WPA3 encryption (or WPA2 if WPA3 unavailable), 5) Basic DHCP monitoring, 6) Quarterly password rotation
Notes: Network segmentation is critical. Cost: <$50 if router supports; $200 for new router if needed. Major security improvement.

Risk Statement: Server hardware failure or crash due to age and lack of redundancy leading to loss of all business data: menu, inventory, customer records, extended operational downtime
Asset: Server (stores all business data)
Threat Actor: Hardware failure (wear and tear, age), environmental failure (overheating, power surge, physical damage)
Vulnerability: Old server (7+ years), no redundancy, no backup process, no UPS (uninterruptible power supply), storage device at end-of-life, staff report unusual noises from server
Impact Description: All business data lost permanently (menu, inventory, customer loyalty points), unable to process orders/payments, extended downtime (days/weeks), customer churn, potential business closure
Current Controls: Server is old but still running; staff do manual backups occasionally (inconsistent), no offsite backup, no recovery tested
Control Gaps: No automated backup; no offsite backup; no redundancy; no UPS; no disaster recovery plan; no regular backup testing
Recommended Controls: 1) Implement daily automated backups to external USB drive, 2) Store backup offsite (in secure location away from cafe), 3) Test backup recovery quarterly, 4) Implement UPS ($200-400) to prevent data loss during power outages, 5) Document disaster recovery procedures, 6) Consider cloud backup (AWS S3, Google Drive for business)
Notes: Data loss would be catastrophic. Backups are cheapest control. Budget: ~$500. Recovery time estimate: 1-2 days with backup; weeks without.

Risk Statement: Customer data breached via compromised staff email account (phishing or weak password) leading to accidental sharing or attacker access to customer data sent via email
Asset: Customer database; business data accessed via email
Threat Actor: External attacker compromising staff email via phishing; or accidental forwarding to wrong recipient; or employee downloading attachment with malware
Vulnerability: Staff email has no MFA; phishing awareness is low; no email encryption; customer data sometimes sent via plain unencrypted email; no Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
Impact Description: Customer data exposed, POPIA notification required, regulatory fine, reputational damage
Current Controls: Some staff have antivirus on computers; Google Workspace (Gmail) has basic email protection
Control Gaps: No MFA on email; no phishing training; no email encryption; no DLP; no email archive; no email recovery
Recommended Controls: 1) Enable MFA on all email accounts (Google Workspace free or built-in), 2) Monthly simulated phishing tests (awareness training), 3) Implement email encryption (PGP/GPG or MailModo), 4) Never send customer data in plain email; use encrypted link instead, 5) Email archive/retention policy, 6) Discuss data security in staff meetings
Notes: MFA and training are quick wins. Cost: $0-100. High ROI (prevents most phishing attacks).

Risk Statement: Trusted vendor (accountant, supplier, payment processor) compromises or mishandles data, leading to data exposure or financial fraud
Asset: Customer data + Financial data (stored in shared Google Drive)
Threat Actor: Trusted but potentially compromised vendor, vendor insider threat, vendor website compromised/hacked, or vendor negligence
Vulnerability: Accountant has broad access to financial data via shared Google Drive, no vendor data processing agreement, no audit trail of vendor access, no access restrictions (accountant can see all data), no vendor risk assessment
Impact Description: Financial data exposed, customer data accessed by accountant inappropriately, reputational damage, compliance violation (no written operator agreement = POPIA s21 gap)
Current Controls: Vendor is long-term trusted partner (10+ years), known personally
Control Gaps: No Data Processing Agreement (DPA); no audit trail; no access restrictions; no vendor assessment; no contract terms about data handling
Recommended Controls: 1) Implement vendor management process: Security questionnaire to vendor, 2) Data Processing Agreement (DPA) required before access, 3) Restrict vendor access (accountant sees ONLY financial data; not customer data), 4) Enable Google Drive audit logs showing who accessed what, 5) Annual vendor risk review, 6) Require vendor insurance (professional liability)
Notes: Balancing convenience (shared access) with security (restricted, monitored). DPA is free template; takes 1 hour to implement.

Risk Statement: Employee malware/ransomware infection via phishing email or infected website leading to ransomware encryption, data theft, or operational disruption
Asset: POS system; Customer database; Staff computers; Payment data
Threat Actor: Malware delivered via phishing email (credential harvester); or infected website; or USB drive from attacker; or ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group
Vulnerability: Staff computers have no centralized antivirus; no email filtering; no endpoint detection; no patch management; staff click links without verification; USB drives accepted from unknown sources
Impact Description: Ransomware encrypts all files, unable to process payments, unable to serve customers, ransom demand ($5K-50K), data theft, operational shutdown for days/weeks
Current Controls: Basic Windows Defender on some computers; not all managed centrally; no email filtering; no policy against USB devices
Control Gaps: No centralized antivirus; no email filtering; no endpoint detection (EDR); no patch management; no device policy; no backup of data (so ransom leverage is high)
Recommended Controls: 1) Implement centralized antivirus (Windows Defender managed centrally or free alternative like Avast), 2) Enable email filtering (Gmail filters free; can block suspicious attachments), 3) Implement patch management (auto-updates for Windows and software), 4) Monthly malware scans, 5) Employee training on phishing/USB risks, 6) No USB devices from unknown sources (policy), 7) Daily backups to external location
Notes: Phishing and malware are top threats to small businesses. Cost: <$500. Employee training is critical.

Risk Statement: Compliance gap: No documented security policies or incident response procedures leading to audit failure, regulatory violation, or ineffective incident response
Asset: Business operations; Compliance/Legal standing
Threat Actor: Regulatory auditor; internal inspection; or incident occurs and organization has no response plan
Vulnerability: No documented incident response plan, no access control policy, no data classification policy, no acceptable use policy, no change management process, no asset inventory
Impact Description: Audit failure, POPIA violation if breach occurs without documented response, ineffective incident response (hours of data loss), regulatory fine, inability to comply with auditor findings
Current Controls: Processes exist informally; staff know what to do but not documented; no training materials
Control Gaps: No formal IR plan; no policies; no documentation; no procedures; no staff training; no testing
Recommended Controls: 1) Create Incident Response Plan (detection, escalation, response, recovery, communication templates), 2) Create Access Control Policy (user provisioning, approval, termination), 3) Create Data Classification Policy (define sensitive vs non-sensitive data), 4) Create Acceptable Use Policy (what employees can/can't do), 5) Document change management process, 6) Annual policy review + staff training
Notes: Documentation is foundation of GRC. Cheap to do now. Expensive to do in emergency. Use templates to reduce effort.

Risk Statement: Ransomware may encrypt critical systems and data while backups fail to restore properly, resulting in prolonged downtime, financial loss, data loss, and operational disruption.
Asset: Critical systems, file servers, databases, backups, recovery process
Threat Actor: External ransomware group, malware operator, compromised insider account
Vulnerability: Untested backups, backups connected to the same network, weak endpoint protection, poor patching, no recovery plan, excessive user privileges
Impact Description: Ransomware impact worsened by  failed backup recovery; ransomware encrypts business data and systems, preventing normal operations; System outage, data loss, service interruption, ransom demand, recovery costs, reputational damage
Current Controls: Daily backup jobs, antivirus, user authentication
Control Gaps: Untested backups; Weak antivirus; No MFA
Recommended Controls: Test backup restoration monthly, keep offline or immutable backups, apply endpoint protection, patch systems, restrict admin privileges, create incident response and disaster recovery plans
Notes: Ransomware encryption leading to operational failure and financial loss and backup failure

Risk Statement: One staff member holds critical knowledge (WiFi password, vendor contacts, customer records access) and if she departs, the cafe faces operational disruption and data access loss
Asset: WiFi access, vendor knowledge, customer database
Threat Actor: Employee departure, sudden illness, resignation
Vulnerability: No documentation of passwords, no contacts backup, knowledge held by one person only
Likelihood (L/M/H/C): Medium (people take time off/leave, leave jobs)
Impact Category: Operational, Financial, Confidential, no off-boarding audit
Impact Description: Business disruption (no WiFi - can't process payments, financial loss), missing vendor contact (can't order supplies)
Current Controls: One person knows password (weak)
Control Gaps: No documentation, no backup person trained, no password backup
Recommended Controls: Document WiFi password in secure location (password manager), Train others on WiFi reset, Document key vendor contacts, Cross-train staff on critical functions
Risk Treatment: Mitigate (Implement controls to reduce likelihood of disruption)
Notes: Train other staff members on password reset;

Risk Statement: Staff laptop containing customer loyalty data or financial information is lost or stolen from cafe, vehicle, or employee's home, resulting in customer exposure and regulatory notification
Asset: Employee laptop, stored documents, customer records, internal files
Threat Actor: Opportunistic thief, unauthorized 3rd party
Vulnerability: No full-disk encryption, weak login password, local storage of sensitive files, no remote wipe capability, poor asset tracking
Likelihood (L/M/H/C): Medium (Laptops taken home, left in vehicles, or lost at cafe events)
Impact Description: Customer data may be exposed (names,email, payment history), reputational damage, potential fraud, regulatory notification, customer churn
Current Controls: Local storage of assets (laptop), password (weak), Staff have Google Workspace accounts (some encryption)
Control Gaps: No remote data wipe capability, no full-disk encryption, weak password, no backup of sensitive data
Recommended Controls: Enable full-disk encryption on all laptops (Windows BitLocker or Mac FileVault), Implement strong passwords (minimum 12 characters), Enable "Find My Device" (locate/wipe stolen laptop), Store sensitive data on encrypted USB only; not laptop hard drive, Set laptop to lock after 15 minutes of inactivity, Keep asset inventory (know which staff has laptops)
Risk Treatment: Backup sensitive data, keep regular inventory
Notes: Enable remote wipe capability and "Find My Device"

Risk Statement: A customer orders food/drink, staff accidentally includes an allergen (gluten, diary, etc). Customer has allergic reaction. Cafe is liable for medical costs and lawsuit.
Asset: Customer health, financial assets, cafe reputation
Threat Actor: Staff mistake, allergen cross-contamination
Vulnerability: No allergen tracking system, no staff training on allergies
Impact Description: Serious injuries, lawsuit, business closure
Current Controls: Basic food safety training; menu disclaimers; allergen labelling, standardized recipes
Control Gaps: No formal training on food allergies; no allergen tracking system; under-staffed (staff gets overwhelmed and makes mistake)
Recommended Controls: Implement allergen tracking system; regularly train staff on allergens; implement physical controls (separate equipment and cleaning stations)
Notes: Allergen tracking failure leading to food/drink safety/poisoning

Risk Statement: Cafe is in high crime rate area and a burglar breaks in after hours. Steals cash from register, office safe, and equipment. No CCTV; no alarm system; no security/police response
Asset: Cash; equipment; building
Threat Actor: Burglar; opportunistic thief
Vulnerability: No lock on office; no alarm; no camera; no security system
Likelihood (L/M/H/C): Medium (Location is semi-visible; no current security = attractive target; local crime data)
Impact Description: Retail theft is common in hospitality; cafe is located in high crime rate area, poor police/security response
Current Controls: Night security, basic office safe/register; cash saved on site; basic physical security (locks)
Control Gaps: Security systems (Alarm / CCTV); poor cash handling procedures (bank); inadequate security
Recommended Controls: Install security systems (CCTV, alarm), daily bank deposit, upgrade the surface, physical security hardening
Notes: Cash theft / Physical adequate security leading to burglary

Risk Statement: Coffee supplier accidentally sends contaminated beans (mold, foreign objects). Cafe uses beans; customers get sick.
Asset: Customer health, product quality, cafe reputation
Threat Actor: Supplier negligence, contaminated delivery
Vulnerability: No quality check process before using new shipment
Impact Description: Customer consumes contaminated coffee resulting in illness; potential lawsuit; brand damage
Current Controls: General food safety practices; supplier selection; casual visual inspection
Control Gaps: Over reliance on supplier; no traceability/batch tracking; no formal receiving inspection; lack of specific training
Recommended Controls: Formal receiving checks, batch and lot tracking, recall and incident protocol, staff quality control training, supplier requirements and agreements
Notes: Supply chain contamination

Risk Statement: Disgruntled / criminal minded employee who is facing financial difficulties steals money from the cash register / office safe or products to sell or use leading to financial loss and operation disruption
Asset: Cash; business operations; products
Threat Actor: Compromised / opportunistic employee; external buyer; competitor
Vulnerability: No CCTV; inadequate security systems; standard POS drawer that locks with key; over-permission access to cash register; high and dubious competition
Likelihood (L/M/H/C): Medium (high staff turnover and new hires are always vetted thoroughly)
Impact Description: Inadequate safe security, product availability
Current Controls: Office safe, cash register, product warehouse / station
Control Gaps: No CCTV (no evidence); cash register / office safe access availability; safe upgrade; warehouse accessibility
Recommended Controls: Safe upgrade; audit logging (who had access to the cash register at a specific timeframe); separation of duties; install CCTV; physical hardening (doors and locks)
Notes: Employee theft/product

Risk Statement: Owner/staff work in an unhealthy and disease infested environment leading to food contamination and illness; persistently disregards regulatory compliance
Asset: Labour law; health code; environmental agreements
Threat Actor: Owner/staff negligence; over-helming customers; regulatory inspectors
Vulnerability: Weak regulatory enforcement; bribery and corruption; low competition; poorness of locals
Impact Description: Poor regulatory inspection and enforcement; no options for the locals/community
Current Controls: Basic food handling controls; basic licensing; basic understanding and interpretation of labour laws and health practices; basic/initial training
Control Gaps: Lack of ongoing training; no documented policies; no internal auditing; no compliance tracking
Recommended Controls: Document on onboarding and training, assign a compliance officer, monthly internal audits, establish a compliance calendar
Notes: Health and food safety regulations

Risk Statement: A failure in food safety protocols leads to a customer food poisoning incident, which rapidly escalates into a viral social media backlash, resulting in severe reputational damage, loss of community trust, and  a significant drop in revenue
Asset: Customer health, cafe reputation, community trust, revenue, basic food safety
Threat Actor: Owner/staff negligence; disgruntled/social media-freak employee
Vulnerability: No quality check process; basic staff training on food handling procedures; informal social media presence
Impact Description: Staff mistakenly sells contaminated/maggot-filled food to customer; Customer posts online the food; reputational damage; loss in revenue
Current Controls: Basic customer service, standard food safety, informal social media presence
Control Gaps: No active monitoring; no crisis communication plan; no designated spoke-person; no "Take if Offline" strategy
Recommended Controls: Social media monitoring; develop a crisis response protocol; refund/compensation policy; root cause remediation
Notes: Food poisoning incident; social media backlash

Risk Statement: Critical operational equipment (espresso machine, refrigerator) unexpectedly breaks down during peak service hours, resulting in an inability to serve core menu items, significant loss of immediate revenue, potential food spoilage, and customer dissatisfaction
Asset: Equipment (espresso machine, refrigerator), perishable food inventory, daily revenue
Threat Actor: Power failure (electricity); aged equipment
Vulnerability: Equipment aging (wear and tear); lack of preventative maintenance; single point of failure (no backup machines); lack of environmental monitoring
Impact Description: Aged equipment failure, food spoilage, financial loss, reputational damage
Current Controls: Daily cleaning, warranties, ad-hoc repairs
Control Gaps: No contingency plan; no environmental monitoring; single point of failure; lack of preventative maintenance; no service level agreement
Recommended Controls: Stock critical spare parts; preventative maintenance contract; contingency menu/operations; emergency vendor list; equipment replacement fund
Notes: Equipment failure leading to daily revenue loss, food spoilage and cafe reputation

Risk Statement: A customer slips falls on a wet or improperly maintained floor, resulting in a serious physical injury, a premises liability lawsuit, medical costs, and negative publicity for the cafe
Asset: Customer health and safety, the cafe's reputation, financial capital
Threat Actor: Wet floor, improperly maintained floor, smooth floor tiled
Vulnerability: Poor visibility of wet areas; smooth flooring materials; lack of immediate spill response during busy hours; wet shoes from rainy weather
Likelihood (L/M/H/C): High (liquid spillage is common in cafes)
Impact Description: Customer injured due to wet/improperly maintained floor resulting in legal notification, financial loss, and cafe brand reputation
Current Controls: Basic cleaning; reactive cleanup; basic/poor staff training skills
Control Gaps: No warning signs; delayed response; weather hazards
Recommended Controls: Mandatory warning signs; clean as you go policy; weather mats (heavy-duty, absorbent floor mats); general liability insurance
Notes: Improperly maintained or wet floor due causing customer slippage, resulting in injuries; financial loss and brand damage
